accessibility_walkthrough: keyboard, focus, live status and 320px reflow passed; no conformance claim
main_findings: The common adapter lifecycle is viable without a universal domain grammar.
Validity must remain separate from correctness or review.
Renderer and runtime state can remain disposable.
Protected validation needs an explicit trusted-host location.
Sandboxed-worker is too vague to express security assurance.
Reference implementations can validate contracts while being rejected as production dependencies.
next_work: Revise the prototype contracts to version 0.2 using accepted amendments.
Run a separate third-party library bake-off behind the unchanged adapter boundary.
Design a production-grade untrusted-code execution and protected-test architecture.
Use the validated lifecycle in the pedagogical configuration taxonomy and product domain model.
